     8	/-!
     9	# `RestrictedChartFibre` is inhabited, and where the content of antecedent 1 actually sits
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` repairs the route to `IsChartUniv` — antecedent 1 of
    12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — by demanding the fibre datum at the **restricted** chart.  Its
    13	own "honest limits" section then recorded the thing it could not settle:
    14	
    15	> an inhabitant at `V = ⊥` was **attempted and not obtained** in this session … the `sq` field
    16	> … needs `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a₁))` over an empty base.  That is the
    17	> triviality of `picEt` over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent
    18	> from the tree.
    19	
    20	**That pricing was wrong, and the error was in the reduction rather than in the census.**  The
    21	`sq` goal is an equality of two elements of `(pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S)` at an *empty* test
    22	`S`, and `pic0SigmaSheaf` is a **sheaf**.  A sheaf's value at an object covered by the empty
    23	sieve is terminal, so the goal is closed with no fact about `picEt` at all:
    24	
    25	* `Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology` (mathlib, `Sites/Pretopology.lean`) — stated exactly for
    26	  `[IsEmpty X]`;
    27	* `Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover` (mathlib, `Sites/Sheaf.lean`).
    28	
    29	The `congr 1` that peeled the Σ-component and named `pic0Subgroup` as the residue is what made
    30	a free goal look like a missing lemma.  Recorded because the prose pricing outlived the check.
    31	
    32	## What this file establishes
    33	
    34	* `pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty` — the sheaf value at an empty test is a subsingleton.
    35	  Three lines, no `picEt` input, no geometry.
    36	* `restrictedChartFibre_bot` — **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` is inhabited,
    37	  unconditionally**: for every `rep`, `m`, `Z`, `hdeg`.  So the class is non-empty and the
    38	  unmeasured-inhabitation risk `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` flagged against itself (and that
    39	  `ChartTyping` and `IsChartLocusFibre` carried) is discharged for this class.
    40	* `isChartUniv_bot` — hence `IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg ⊥` holds with **no hypothesis**.
    41	* `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_bot` — the same construction for an **arbitrary** chart
    42	  map, which is what the `⊥` witness really rests on: a lane that gets `hf` at `⊥` has learned
    43	  nothing about its own chart.
    44	* `range_subset_range_top_ι`,
    45	  `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_restrictedChartFibre_top` and
    46	  `not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective` — the opposite end of the interval.
    47	* `restrictedChartFibre_top_iff` — at `V = ⊤` the class is **equivalent** to
    48	  `IsChartLocusFibre`, which retires the latter as an independent obligation and supplies the
    49	  converse `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:55` claims exists under a name nothing defines.
    50	
    51	## The consequence, and it is a statement about the seam rather than about this file
    52	
    53	`isChartUniv_bot` says antecedent 1 **carries no content at `V = ⊥`**.  That is not a defect of
    54	the repair, and it is *not* a vacuity of the coupled assembly — because the coverage side is
    55	refuted at the same value:
    56	
    57	* `not_coverageContainment_bot` — the `hcov` hypothesis of
    58	  `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre_of_coverage` at `V = ⊥` is **false** as soon as
    59	  some test has a point.  Its witness `x` would have range inside `Set.range ((⊥).ι.base) = ∅`
    60	  while `t ∈ W` exhibits a point of the source.
    61	
    62	## Both ends of the `V`-interval, and why the coupling has an interior
    63	
    64	The two endpoints are priced in **opposite** directions, and that is the file's main content:
    65	
    66	* at `V = ⊥`: `hf` is **free** (`restrictedChartFibre_bot`), and coverage's containment is
    67	  **impossible** (`not_coverageContainment_bot`);
    68	* at `V = ⊤`: coverage's containment is **free** (`range_subset_range_top_ι`), and `hf` is the
    69	  **unrestricted certificate** (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_…_top`).
    70	
    71	At `⊤` the restricted datum returns exactly the certificate the restriction was introduced to
    72	avoid — the one `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
    73	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` assert to be false for the Abel chart.  So the
    74	restriction is not a formality that a lane could undo by taking `V` large.
    75	
    76	Hence **no endpoint discharges the assembly**, and any `V` that works must be a proper
    77	intermediate open (`not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective` makes the `⊤` end an outright
    78	refutation, conditional on the `abel-noninj` fork).  That is what the chart locus is for, and it
    79	is why CHART-U(b)'s openness is a real obligation rather than bookkeeping: neither an `hf` lane
    80	nor a coverage lane can retreat to a convenient `V`.
    81	
    82	**What this is NOT, and an earlier draft of this header claimed otherwise** (`I-1012`, filed by a
    83	fresh-context review of this file).  The two endpoints are **not** a non-vacuity check for the
    84	coupled assembly.  Non-vacuity of a pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` needs a `V` where both hold — or a
    85	refutation at every `V` — and two *bad* values of `V` supply neither.  The pair still has **no
    86	measured inhabitant at any `V`**, and nothing here excludes it being unsatisfiable everywhere.
    87	What *is* discharged is inhabitation of `RestrictedChartFibre` alone, at `⊥`, which is strictly
    88	weaker.  The sentence above ("any `V` that works must be a proper intermediate open") is a
    89	conditional and must not be read as an existence claim.  So `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre`
    90	was not the assembly's non-vacuity check (`I-0937`), and neither is this file; the assembly's
    91	non-vacuity is **open**.
    92	
    93	A further limit the endpoints do not reach: at `V = ⊥` the *instance* form
    94	`pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` goes through with `huniv` supplied free by
    95	`restrictedChartFibre_bot`, leaving the `IsLocallySurjective` instance binder as the sole
    96	remaining antecedent.  `not_coverageContainment_bot` constrains the `hcov` *spelling* of coverage,
    97	not that instance binder — so it does not by itself rule out a `⊥`-based route through the
    98	instance version.
    99	
   100	**What is still NOT closed, stated plainly.**  `rep` remains a hypothesis with no producer, so
   101	`IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it; `hcov` at a useful `V` has no producer; and
   102	nothing here produces a chart at a `V` other than `⊥`.  No antecedent of
   103	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is discharged by this file.  What is discharged is the
   104	*satisfiability question* about the class, plus the sharp localisation of the remaining
   105	obligation.
   106	-/

   117	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   118	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}

   122	noncomputable section
   123	
   124	/-! ## The empty test, from the sheaf axiom -/
   125	
   126	/-- **The Σ-sheaf is trivial on an empty test** — by the sheaf axiom, not by any property of
   127	`picEt`.
   128	
   129	The empty sieve covers an empty scheme (`Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`), and a sheaf's
   130	value at an object with a `⊥` cover is terminal (`Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover`); a terminal
   131	object of `Type u` is a subsingleton.
   132	
   133	This is the declaration `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` priced as "the triviality of `picEt`
   134	over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent from the tree".  Note what
   135	does *not* appear: no `picEt`, no `pic0Subgroup`, no `relPic`, no curve geometry.  The residue
   136	was named after a `congr 1` had already thrown away the structure that makes it free. -/
   137	theorem pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsEmpty S] :
   138	    Subsingleton ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S)) :=
   139	  (Equiv.subsingleton_congr
   140	    ((Types.isTerminalEquivIsoPUnit _
   141	      (Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover (pic0SigmaSheaf C) S
   142	        (Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology S))).toEquiv)).mpr inferInstance
   143	
   144	/-- The carrier of the bottom open of a scheme is empty.  Stated as an instance because the
   145	`isInitialOfIsEmpty` applications below need it by synthesis. -/
   146	instance isEmpty_coe_bot_opens (T : Scheme.{u}) : IsEmpty ((⊥ : T.Opens) : Scheme.{u}) :=
   147	  ⟨fun x => x.2⟩
   148	
   149	/-! ## Inhabitation of the restricted datum -/
   150	
   151	/-- **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` is inhabited, with no hypotheses beyond the data the
   152	statement mentions.**
   153	
   154	Take `W := ⊥` as well.  Then:
   155	
   156	* `r` is the unique map out of an empty scheme (`isInitialOfIsEmpty`);
   157	* `sq` is an equality of natural transformations out of `yoneda.obj ↑⊥`; after `ext S x` the
   158	  morphism `x : S.unop ⟶ ↑⊥` forces `S.unop` empty, and
   159	  `pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty` closes it;
   160	* `exists_factor` is free: `v : S ⟶ ↑⊥` forces `S` empty, hence initial, so the factoring map
   161	  and both compatibilities are unique.
   162	
   163	**Why this is worth landing rather than just knowing.**  `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean` said a
   164	lane picking up that row "should produce that witness first … it decides whether the repair is
   165	real".  It does, and the answer is yes: the class is not empty, so the repaired route to
   166	`IsChartUniv` is not a route to an uninhabitable hypothesis. -/
   167	theorem restrictedChartFibre_bot {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   168	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   169	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   170	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   171	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
   172	    RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg ⊥ := by
   173	  intro T g
   174	  refine ⟨⟨⊥, isInitialOfIsEmpty.to _, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
   175	  · ext S x
   176	    have : IsEmpty (S.unop : Scheme.{u}) := x.base.hom.1.isEmpty
   177	    exact (pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty (C := C) S.unop).elim _ _
   178	  · intro S v w _
   179	    have : IsEmpty S := v.base.hom.1.isEmpty
   180	    exact ⟨isInitialOfIsEmpty.to _, isInitialOfIsEmpty.hom_ext _ _,
   181	      isInitialOfIsEmpty.hom_ext _ _⟩

 * subset_chart0_or_disjoint_chart0 / _chart1_ : the dichotomy the shape imposes on the divisor.

WHAT IT SETTLES. The lane's obligation is chart-trace closedness, a property of the system and the
two pinned charts alone. Refining the cover cannot help (it adds constraints while the union of the
traces is fixed), so leak-image route (b) is dead; and the tube/idempotent machinery cannot
manufacture it, so leak-image route (a) is exactly chart-avoid. The lane is therefore a chart-design
problem, not a fibre-analysis problem.

Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean (commit 40f357de8) — THE SATISFIABILITY VERDICT.
 * subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak : leak-freeness makes the piece trace CLOSED
   and the piece is OPEN, so the trace is clopen in the support; a preconnected support forces it
   empty or total. Swallow-or-miss is therefore not an extra hypothesis for a connected divisor —
   it is what leak-freeness already says.
 * supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected : IsPreconnected supportLocus plus leak-freeness at
   every piece implies supportLocus subset V_0 OR supportLocus subset V_1. No nonemptiness needed.
 * not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected : contrapositive — a connected divisor confined
   to neither pinned chart admits NO leak-free adaptation, over any base, after any shrink.

SO: IsCertified is satisfiable for a connected divisor only if the divisor avoids pi^{-1}(0) or
pi^{-1}(infinity). Seven rounds were spent proving hypotheses of an interface whose satisfiability
had never been checked.

Picard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean (commit 5651710d6) — THE KEYSTONE, closing Ground's I-0334.
 * IsAffineOpen.isClosed_zeroLocus_inter_of_finite_quotient — the converse of the abstract finiteness
   engine: Module.Finite makes Spec(Gamma(V)/I) -> Spec R finite hence universally closed; it factors
   through X and X -> Spec R is separated, so the first leg is universally closed
   (UniversallyClosed.of_comp_of_isSeparated) and its range — the trace — is closed.
 * supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength / supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength — clause (c1)
   and leak-freeness are the SAME condition at a piece. This is the equivalence I-0209 asserted and
   nobody had proved.
 * supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified — the verdict for IsCertified itself.
Axioms of the keystone: exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

     8	/-!
     9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
    12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
    13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
    14	CERT-Σ-gated.
    15	
    16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
    17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
    18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
    19	
    20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
    21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
    22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
    23	
    24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
    25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
    26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
    27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
    28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
    29	
    30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
    31	
    32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
    33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
    34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
    35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
    36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
    37	
    38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
    39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
    40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
    41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
    42	
    43	## Main declarations
    44	
    45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
    46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
    47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
    48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
    50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
    51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
    52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
    53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
    54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
    55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
    56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
    57	  this route.
    58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
    59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
    60	-/

   112	variable (C) in
   113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
   114	
   115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
   116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
   117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
   118	
   119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
   120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
   121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
   122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
   123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
   124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
   125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
   126	
   127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
   128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
   129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
   130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   131	    where
   132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
   133	  W : T.Opens
   134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
   135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
   136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
   137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
   139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
   140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
   141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   142	
   143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
   144	
   145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
   146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
   147	
   148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
   149	pullback of presheaves.
   150	
   151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
   152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
   153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
   154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
   155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
   156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
   157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
   158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
   162	      φ.app S) D.sq
   163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
   164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
   166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
   167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
   168	    intro v w hvw
   169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
   171	
   172	end ChartFibrePresented
   173	
   174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
   175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
   176	
   177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map

   179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
   180	each.
   181	
   182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
   183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
   184	
   185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
   186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
   187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
   188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
   189	
   190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
   191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
   192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the

   195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
   196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
   198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
   199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
   200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_

   202	    inferInstance⟩
   203

   205	
   206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
   207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
   208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
   209	
   210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
   211	
   212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
   213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied

   216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
   217	
   218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
   219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
   220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)

   222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),

   226	
   227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**

   229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not

   231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
   232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),

   236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
   237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)

/-- **The `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data** of the two pinned charts of the relative
curve (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): `m₀ + m₁` basic-open generators with partition
witnesses. The DAT-1 datum `BasicOpenCoverData` carries `Type u` index fields and hence
lives in `Type (u+1)`; this `Fin`-indexed form is the `Type u` carrier a functor value
can quotient. -/
structure FinCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
  /-- The number of chart-0 pieces. -/
  m₀ : ℕ
  /-- The number of chart-1 pieces. -/
  m₁ : ℕ
  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
  h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
  h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
  a₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
  a₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
  partition₀ : ∑ j : Fin m₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
  partition₁ : ∑ j : Fin m₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1

namespace FinCoverData

variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)

/-- The gluing index of the adaptation, `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/
abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m₀ ⊕ Fin D.m₁

/-- The pieces: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
    (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))

@[simp]
lemma pieces_inl (j : Fin D.m₀) :
    D.pieces (Sum.inl j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma pieces_inr (j : Fin D.m₁) :
    D.pieces (Sum.inr j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) := rfl

/-- The chart-0 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₀ᴿ`. -/
lemma cover₀ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ≤
    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₀, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) :=

/-!
# Locally certified divisor families: the `DivFamZar` carrier (DD-2 stage S5b)

The Addendum-2 repair of the divisor-functor carrier (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`,
Addendum 2): the globally-certified `DivFam` is not a Zariski sheaf — the diagonal
divisor over `Γ(C \ pt)` is certifiable on a basic-open cover of the base but carries
no global certificate — so the faithful functor value is the **locally certified**
quotient `DivFamZar`. The generic germ-regularity engines live in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarKit`.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertified` — the Addendum-2 frozen pin: a span-⊤ family
  `g : Fin m → R` with certified divisor families over `Localization.Away (g i)`
  divisor-equal to the pulled system; `hreg` is discharged by the Kit's open-immersion
  lemma, with the S4 instance provided by `haveI`.
* `IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq` — the pin respects divisor equality.
* `CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified` — a global certificate is a local one
  (trivial cover `g = ![1]`; the certified part is `mapAlg` to `Localization.Away 1`,
  whose equations ARE the pulled system on the nose).
* `IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — **the mapAlg-hreg
  engine**: a locally certified system has regular pulled equations along the
  comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'` — regularity is germ-local, each germ
  sits over a chart `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` of `R'`, where the
  local certificate's regularity transports through its `DivEq` and the landed
  certificate-based pullback regularity.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar` — the quotient of locally certified systems by
  `DivEq`, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `picClass`, and `DivFam.toZar`.

Total `DivFamZar.mapAlg` and the Zariski keystones are
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg` / `…ZarGlue`.
-/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **The Addendum-2 frozen pin** (`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): a
local-equation system on the relative curve is *locally certified* in degree `n` if
some span-⊤ family `g : Fin m → R` carries certified divisor families over the
localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` that are divisor-equal to the pulled system.
The pullback's regularity hypothesis is discharged once and for all by the Kit's
open-immersion lemma — the comparison of an away localization is an open immersion
(the S4 instance, provided by `haveI`). -/
def IsLocallyCertified (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin m,
      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) π n,
        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))

variable {C R π}

/-- **The locally certified pin respects divisor equality**: the local `DivEq`s
transport through `divEq_pullback` (regularity along the chart immersions is free). -/
theorem IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d' := by
  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
      h _ _)⟩

/-- **A global certificate is a local one** (the trivial cover `g = ![1]`): the
certified part over `Localization.Away (1 : R)` is `mapAlg` of the family, whose
equations are the pulled system on the nose (`pulledEquations` IS the pullback along
the comparison; the regularity proofs are proof-irrelevant). -/
theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : IsLocallyCertified C R π n F.eqns := by
  refine ⟨1, fun _ => (1 : R), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
  · have hrange : Set.range (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : R)) = {1} := Set.range_const
    rw [hrange, Ideal.span_singleton_one]
  · haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (1 : R))) :=
      isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (1 : R)) 1
    exact ⟨F.mapAlg (Localization.Away (1 : R)) n,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩

/-! ## The mapAlg-hreg engine -/

section MapAlgHreg

variable {n : ℕ} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']

/-- **The mapAlg-hreg engine** (S5b): a locally certified system has regular pulled
equations along the comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'`. Regularity is
germ-local on the curve: the charts `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` cover
`relCurve C R'` by open immersions; over each, the composite comparison factors
through the certified chart `Localization.Away (g i)`, where the certificate's
pullback regularity (`DivisorAdaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors`)
transports through the recorded `DivEq`. -/
theorem IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    (hloc : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d)
    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)

     9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
    12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
    13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
    14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
    15	index per point of `T`".

    17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
    18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
    19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
    20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
    21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
    22	connection is what this file supplies.
    23	
    24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
    25	
    26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
    27	
    28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
    29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
    30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
    31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
    32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
    33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
    34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
    35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
    36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
    37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
    38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
    39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
    40	
    41	## Main declarations
    42	
    43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
    44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve

    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the

pinned charts.** This refutes, at the level of the pieces, the shape the `tube-fibre` leaf
of the certificate lane was aiming at.

A support point `z` of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in a chart-0 piece and a chart-1 piece, and those are
distinct — so two distinct pieces meet the support, no matter how the cover is refined. -/
theorem not_exists_unique_support_piece
    {z : relCurve C R} (hz : z ∈ d.supportLocus)
    (hz₀ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)
    (hz₁ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁)
    (j₀ : A.index)
    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
      ∀ y : relCurve C R, y ∈ A.pieces j → y ∉ d.supportLocus) : False :=
  A.supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated
    (A.forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece j₀ hother) hz hz₀ hz₁

/-! ## The certificate -/

/-- **The certificate of a support-separated adaptation.** With the off-diagonal overlap
colengths vanishing, the equalizer is the whole product, the Čech difference is zero, and
both flat-cokernel clauses hold automatically.  What is left is exactly the (c1) data —
each chart-local colength finite projective over `R` — plus the constant-rank reading,
which for the product is the sum of the per-piece ranks.

This is the shape the pointwise gate can consume: no kernel-spanning hypothesis, and no
flatness of a Čech cokernel over a possibly nonreduced base. -/
theorem isCertified_of_separated {n : ℕ} [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
    (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      ∑ᶠ j : A.index, Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) (A.colength j) p = n) :
    A.IsCertified n := by
  classical
  haveI := hfin
  haveI := hproj
  haveI : ∀ j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := fun _ =>
    Module.Flat.of_projective
  have htop := A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
  have hequiv : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd := A.gluedTopEquiv' htop

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarLeak

/-!
# The chart trace is what no-leak really asks for

The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise no-leak clause, which is
emptiness of the leak locus, which is closedness of the piece trace
`supportLocus ∩ pieces j` (`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`), which
is clopen-ness of that trace inside the support (`isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`).

This file records the consequence that had been missed for the whole lifetime of the lane:
**the per-piece clause cannot be produced piece by piece.**  A `FinCoverData` carries a
partition of unity on each pinned chart, so the chart-`b` pieces cover the *whole* pinned
chart `V_b` — hence the union of their traces is the whole chart trace
`supportLocus ∩ V_b`.  A finite union of closed sets is closed, so

> no-leak at every chart-`b` piece **forces** `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed in the
> relative curve, i.e. the chart trace to be clopen in the support.

That is a property of the *system and the pinned charts alone*: no choice of adaptation, and
no shrinking of the base, can produce no-leak for a system whose chart trace is not closed.
It is therefore the honest gate of the lane, and it replaces the refuted `tube-fibre`
framing (put the support inside one piece — impossible once the support meets both charts,
`not_exists_unique_support_piece`) and the refuted separated framing
(`DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`) with a single geometric statement about the divisor.

Read positively, it says where to aim, but the converse is **not** the mirror image and this
file does not claim it: closed chart traces alone do not produce a leak-free adaptation.  What
does is `DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`, and it needs two further inputs — the support inside
the chart *overlap* `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, and a chart-principality datum making the two pinned charts
themselves legal pieces.  Both are recorded there and on the roadmap
(`…certificate.chart-avoid`, `…certificate.swallow-adapt`).

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion` /
  `…_chart₁_…` — the chart trace is the finite union of the chart's piece traces.
* `DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₀_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty`
  and its chart-1 twin — no-leak at every piece of a chart forces the chart trace closed.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak` —
  the assembler-shaped form: the `hnoLeak` hypothesis of
  `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` forces both chart traces closed.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₀` — the
  obstruction, contrapositive: a system with a non-closed chart-0 trace admits **no**
  adaptation satisfying the assembler's no-leak clause.
-/
